runtime.execution: Ingress/API, replicated log/partition processors, durable journal/state/outbox, service invoker HTTP protocol and SQL introspection. User code runs separately in SDK service deployments.
runtime.service_boundary: Owns scheduling/storage/replay/service control plane. Arconaut would consume this boundary, not govern its shared fleet. User service/provider/OS effects remain external.

summary: durable invocation, state, RPC/wait and administrative pause/replay/deployment/query machinery

inspection.scope: ingress call/send/visibility, v4 invoker journal replay/completion proposal, state-machine journal/state/outbox, pause/cancel/resume/deployment fencing, query schema/retention and direct lifecycle/idempotency/fencing tests
inspection.limits: Not a full replication/fleet correctness audit; no server launch/test occurred. External SDK closures and semantic replay compatibility are not certified by protocol compatibility.

actions.name: Ingress service/object/workflow call and send
actions.input: Target handler/key, body/headers/idempotency and optional send delay
actions.output: Call result or202 invocation ID/execution time/Accepted|PreviouslyAccepted
actions.lifecycle: Server invocation outlives submitting client; call delay disallowed; sends recorded/scheduled
actions.authority: Public handler schema at ingress; service fleet owns work

actions.name: SDK v4 run completion/journal replay
actions.input: Invocation attempt, stored journal/state and SDK serialized result proposal
actions.output: Replay frames, completion notifications and exact journal entries
actions.lifecycle: Fresh service attempt replays recorded results; arbitrary external action precedes settlement
actions.authority: Registered SDK deployment, VM protocol and partition service

actions.name: State and CallCommand/OneWayCallCommand
actions.output: Stored state, outbox invocation and correlated invocation-ID result
actions.lifecycle: Partition state-machine scope; external systems beyond Restate are not in transaction
actions.authority: Service handler context; runtime owns state/log/outbox

actions.name: PauseInvocation / ResumeInvocation with deployment patch
actions.input: Invocation ID; optional pinned/latest deployment and run_at
actions.lifecycle: Journal retained; abort current attempt, fence stragglers, replay later; protocol compatibility only
actions.authority: Admin/server control, not consumer-wide service shutdown

actions.name: CancelInvocation
actions.output: Appended for active waits; Done for queued/scheduled; AlreadyCompleted/NotFound
actions.lifecycle: Active cancellation is a durable signal, not guarantee all external activity stopped

actions.name: POST /query
actions.output: Streaming rows, raw journal bytes/decoded entries/events/state views
actions.lifecycle: Retained platform data only; availability/rate limits; journal purge reduces history

actions.name: PurgeJournal completed invocation
actions.output: Dropped journal, retained completion with zero journal length
actions.lifecycle: Active invocation rejected; irreversible original journal deletion by retention/admin

authority.detail: Public ingress rejects private handlers; admin lifecycle/query controls operate platform state. No model/operator approval policy or permissions for arbitrary handler OS effects supplied.

evaluation.detail: Direct state-machine and committed-log oracles test pause/abort/state, protocol replacement rejection, literal retained output and stale-attempt fencing. No claim full distributed or arbitrary external-effect conformance.

time_order.detail: Exact journal index, record-created append timestamp and after-journal event index provide platform causal order; external effects/time are outside captured protocol.

evidence.claim: Latest target resolution rejects private handler at public ingress.
Call versus send routing, retained ID/idempotency, delayed schedule and202 acceptance/prior acceptance response.
Attempt starts with state/seed/journal metadata then streams stored journal replay from transaction.
SDK run result decoded into raw notification proposal; this follows external closure execution, not atomic third-party settlement.
Apply notification, append raw journal at exact index/deterministic record timestamp, update invocation status.
User state mutation written through same state-machine context for keyed service target.
Durable call request enqueued into outbox, invocation-ID completion correlated back to caller.
Manual pause preserves journal, aborts running attempt; suspended pause drops wait set for replay recomputation.
Write-time current-attempt fencing token prevents stale effects entering durable log, not external effect settlement.
Cancel signal appended for invoked/suspended/paused; queued/scheduled terminated; response distinguishes Appended/Done/completed/missing.
Replacement deployment must exist/support pinned protocol version; semantic handler program equivalence is not checked here.
Deployment patch resolved at command log position, pinned ID updated and paused/suspended invocation resumed.
POST/query executes SQL, JSON or Arrow streaming results; availability/errors/rate limit handled.
Journal query exposes indices/targets/raw binary/version2 JSON/append timestamps.
Events carry invocation ID, after-journal index, timestamp/type/event JSON.
Only completed invocation journal can be dropped; result status survives with length/commands reset.
Pause state-machine test checks Accepted+abort action and stored Paused status.
Literal protocol-incompatible/unknown/unpinned replacement errors.
Completed idempotent call produces stored literal123 response; this range does not independently count actual external effects.
Controlled attempts/pause/stragglers test reads committed log and asserts only current attempt effects appended.

tests.oracle: State-machine environment asserts exact reply/action and persistent Paused state; does not assert third-party OS work ended.
Literal protocol-incompatible/unknown/unpinned errors; protocol oracle does not validate changed workflow semantic replay.

tests.focus: Stored result on completed keyed invocation
tests.oracle: Known stored123 result expected for repeated idempotency key; scoped to state machine, not external payment/model request exactly once.
Distinguishable current/stale effects with pause/resume; reads committed log and asserts only accepted current effects. Direct fault oracle, not physical external cancellation.

strengths: Durable replay, result identity, state/outbox and explicit invocation lifecycle are separated in source.
Current-attempt fencing tested by reading actual committed log against distinguishable stale/current effects.
Query exposes raw journal plus causal event links rather than only aggregate logs.
limits: External closure/provider/OS effects are not atomically settled or fully audited by durable protocol.
Deployment protocol compatibility does not prove semantic journal replay compatibility.
Cancellation appended/pause accepted is not physical external quiescence; retained journal can be purged.
arconaut_questions: Which client operations can consume durable service identity without transferring shared governor responsibilities into Arconaut?
What replay compatibility, idempotency/reconciliation and outstanding-effect accounting must compiled refit enforce beyond protocol versions?
Can original core audit retain consumed service journal references even after external retention deletes them?
